title: OpenAI o3: Reasoning that Uses Tools
hook: o3 is the first reasoning model that can agentically reach for every ChatGPT tool mid-thought - web search, Python on your files, image input, image generation - and combine them to solve a problem.
key_points: An o-series reasoning model trained to 'think for longer' before responding.
The first reasoning models that can agentically use and combine every ChatGPT tool: web search, Python on uploaded files, visual-input reasoning, and image generation.
OpenAI states o3 makes about 20% fewer major errors than o1 on difficult real-world tasks.
Launched alongside o4-mini, a cost-efficient reasoning model; both are available in the API.
content_html: OpenAI released o3 on April 16, 2025 - an o-series reasoning model trained to think for longer before responding, first previewed back in December 2024. Its defining feature is agentic tool use: o3 and its smaller sibling o4-mini are the first reasoning models that can reach for and combine every tool in ChatGPT while working through a problem.
extra_html:
What's new

Beyond reasoning longer, o3 can agentically use web search, run Python on uploaded files, reason over visual input, and generate images - and chain these together within a single task. OpenAI states that o3 makes about 20% fewer major errors than o1 on difficult real-world tasks. It launched alongside o4-mini, a more cost-efficient reasoning model, and both are available in the API.

Why it matters

Reasoning models had largely thought in isolation; letting o3 call tools mid-reasoning turns it from a better answerer into something closer to an agent that can gather evidence, run code, and inspect images on its own. See OpenAI's announcement for details.

related.title: OpenAI o1: Learning to Reason with Reinforcement Learning
related.hook: OpenAI's o1 lets a model think via a long internal chain-of-thought before answering - spending more compute at inference time visibly improves reasoning.

related.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
related.hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.

related.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
related.hook: Ask a big model to 'think step by step' and its math and logic scores jump. Reasoning was there all along — you just had to ask it to show its work.
